exercise.name: Dumbbell Over Bench Wrist Curl
aliases: Dumbbell wrist curl over a bench

reference.title: Dumbbell Over Bench Wrist Curl
reference.listing: Page could not be read (gymvisual.com blocked by the proxy); movement taken from the exercise name and standard coaching practice
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

breathing.pattern: Exhale as the hands curl up, inhale as they lower.
breathing.cadence: About 1 s up, 0.4 s squeeze, 1.7 s down

prescription.load: Dumbbell load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can control through the full range for every rep with 1-3 reps in reserve (RPE 7-9). Wrist curls need a light dumbbell.
prescription.progression: More reps, then a slower lowering, then a heavier dumbbell (small steps)

cues.text: Kneel facing the side of a flat bench and lean forward from the hips. Lay both forearms across the pad, palms up, wrists just past the far edge; let the dumbbells pull the hands down.
Breathe out and curl the hands up toward you, bending only at the wrists.
Squeeze at the top; the forearms stay flat on the bench.
Breathe in and lower slowly until the wrists are bent back past the edge.
Keep a firm grip at the bottom; repeat.

mistakes.fix: Keep the forearms pinned to the pad; only the hands move.
Lower slowly and pause before curling.
Use a weight you can move through the whole range.

mistakes.mistake: Wrists resting on the edge of the bench
mistakes.fix: Slide forward until the wrists are just past the edge, so the hands can drop and curl freely.

kinematics.norm: Healthy adults used up to about 54 degrees of wrist flexion and 60 degrees of extension in daily tasks, functional range about 40 each way (Ryu 1991); a curl goes a little further, to a comfortable end range without pain (clinical opinion)
Forearms lie flat across the bench and stay still; the wrists just past the edge so the hands move freely (clinical opinion)
Kneel close to the bench and lean forward from the hips so the forearms lie flat on the pad with the upper arms about vertical (clinical opinion)

Slow and controlled, about 1 s up, a short squeeze and 1.5-2 s down (clinical opinion); resistance programmes for the wrist extensors in tendinopathy used 1-4 sets of about 15 reps, with no optimal dose defined (J Hand Ther 2012)

sources.title: GymVisual Dumbbell Over Bench Wrist Curl, video page (movement reference; page not readable here)
Ryu, Cooney, Askew, An and Chao 1991, functional ranges of motion of the wrist joint (J Hand Surg Am 16(3):409-419; 40 adults, biaxial wrist electrogoniometer)
Szymanski, Szymanski, Molloy and Pascoe 2004, effect of 12 weeks of wrist and forearm training on high school baseball players (J Strength Cond Res 18(3):432-440; PubMed 15320673; 43 players)
Effectiveness of different methods of resistance exercises in lateral epicondylosis, a systematic review (J Hand Ther 2012;25(1):5-25; PubMed 22075055; 12 studies)

cautions: Wrist pain or carpal tunnel symptoms: shorten the range at the bottom and use a lighter dumbbell (clinical opinion).
Wrist or elbow pain: use a lighter dumbbell and a shorter range; stop if pain persists (clinical opinion).
Keep the forearms on the bench so the elbows and shoulders stay out of it.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Knee discomfort: kneel on a folded mat, or sit and rest the forearms on the thighs instead.
One arm at a time to focus on control.

muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_r: The wrist flexors (flexor carpi radialis and ulnaris, palmaris longus) curl the hand up; the finger flexors hold the handle. Added wrist and forearm work gave greater wrist and forearm strength gains than the same programme without it (Szymanski 2004).
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_l: The wrist flexors (flexor carpi radialis and ulnaris, palmaris longus) curl the hand up; the finger flexors hold the handle. Added wrist and forearm work gave greater wrist and forearm strength gains than the same programme without it (Szymanski 2004).
muscleNotes.forearm_extensors_r: Work lightly to steady the wrist at the bottom and control the lowering (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.forearm_extensors_l: Work lightly to steady the wrist at the bottom and control the lowering (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.biceps_r: Holds the elbow bent at about a right angle while the forearm rests on the thigh (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.biceps_l: Holds the elbow bent at about a right angle while the forearm rests on the thigh (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.core: Holds the forward lean with a long back.

phases.label: Wrists bent back, forearms on the thighs
